definitions.explanation: A type of persimmon that loses its astringency on the tree and can be eaten raw when ripe, as opposed to the astringent {渋柿|しぶがき}.

examples.japanese: {甘柿|あまがき}⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{生|なま}→生：03509_nama⟧⟦で→で：00502_de⟧⟦{食|た}べられる→食べる：00396_taberu⟧。
examples.english: Sweet persimmons can be eaten raw.
Sweet persimmons grew on the tree in the garden.

examples.japanese: {甘柿|あまがき}⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{渋柿|しぶがき}→渋柿：27688_shibugaki⟧⟦と→と：00512_to⟧⟦{違|ちが}い→違う：01957_chigau⟧、⟦{熟|じゅく}す→熟す：18384_jukusu⟧⟦と→と：00512_to⟧⟦{自然|しぜん}→自然：01423_shizen⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{甘|あま}く→甘い：00617_amai⟧⟦なる→なる：01970_naru⟧。
examples.english: Unlike astringent persimmons, sweet persimmons become sweet naturally as they ripen.

notes:
A persimmon variety that is sweet enough to eat raw once ripe. Contrasted with the astringent ⟦{渋柿|しぶがき}→渋柿：27688_shibugaki⟧, which must have its astringency removed before eating.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {甘柿|あまがき}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{品種|ひんしゅ}→品種：11840_hinshu⟧: varieties of sweet persimmon
- {甘柿|あまがき}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧もぐ: to pick sweet persimmons

SIMILAR WORDS:
- ⟦{渋柿|しぶがき}→渋柿：27688_shibugaki⟧: astringent persimmon — inedible raw until de-astringed or dried
- ⟦{干|ほ}し{柿|がき}→干し柿：28314_hoshigaki⟧: dried persimmon — usually made from ⟦{渋柿|しぶがき}→渋柿：27688_shibugaki⟧
